heroSubtitle: Explore original recipes. Find your next cup.
author: Author
sectionIntro: Original methods, carefully sourced. Browse by equipment, explore an author, or compare recipes side by side.
limit: You can compare up to three recipes.
compareSubtitle: Original parameters, side by side. See the differences clearly.
compareNote: Units are preserved as published. Water volume in mL is not silently converted to mass in g.
compareEmpty: Choose recipes from the library to begin a comparison.
invalidSelection: Some recipes in this link are unavailable, duplicated or exceed the three-recipe limit. Only valid selections are shown.
sourceIntro: Every recipe links to its creator or a publishing partner. Versions remain separate; missing details are shown explicitly.
methodText: Measurements stay in their published units. Equipment filters find matching equipment, not a personal best recipe. Fixed amounts are not automatically scaled.
translationNote: Translations are independently prepared and terminology-checked. The linked original remains the reference; no creator endorsement is implied.
imageNote: Editorial images are AI-generated illustrations, not photographs supplied by the recipe authors.
independent: An independent coffee reference by imycc.
authorsIntro: Explore each author’s published recipes and original sources.
noResults: No recipes match these filters. Try another brewer or clear the filters.
raoWater: About 100 ppm general hardness and 40 ppm alkalinity; the source does not state a reporting basis.
raoPrep: With the valve open, rinse the filter and drain the rinse water. Fit the barrel firmly, add the coffee and level the bed.
derived: Total water is calculated from the source’s dose and stated mass ratio, not a separately published measurement.

instruction.bloom: Add the stated amount to wet the coffee grounds.
instruction.pour: Add the stated amount at the indicated time. The total so far is shown separately.
instruction.pause: Stop pouring until the next step begins.
instruction.close: Close the valve immediately after the first pour.
instruction.open: Open the valve after topping up.
instruction.topup: Pour until the water sits about 1 cm above the grounds.
instruction.pulses: Use short pours to keep the water 1–2 cm above the grounds, continuing to the total water target.
instruction.level: Level the coffee bed before brewing.

kasuya.title: Kasuya’s 4:6 method
kasuya.summary: Five pours, clearly timed. The HARIO-published version of Tetsu Kasuya’s 4:6 method.
kasuya.notes: This is HARIO’s published teaching version, not a reconstruction of the competition brew. Its last two pours begin at 2:10 and 2:40.
kasuya.finish: Remove the dripper at the source’s stated finish time.

hoffmann.title: A better one-cup V60
hoffmann.summary: A small-batch V60 with measured pours, gentle swirls and short pauses.
hoffmann.notes: Freshly boiled water is the recommendation for lighter roasts. The finish time is approximate; the source prioritizes taste over a fixed drawdown time.
hoffmann.finish: Let the water drain through. Some variation in total time is expected.

rao.title: Pulsar starting recipe
rao.summary: Valve-controlled blooming and short pulse pours for the NextLevel Pulsar.
rao.grind: Coarser than hand pour, finer than batch brew
rao.notes: The source outline gives a 45–60 second bloom, while its detailed technique resumes at 45–50 seconds. Both are retained here. Pulse amounts and exact later times are not specified.
rao.finish: The target total brew time is a range. Finish draining within that range as described by the source.
